title: Define provider-neutral structured intelligence contracts
businessObjective: Establish provider-neutral, schema-valid intelligence inputs and results for bounded technical, operational, SEO, and commercial analysis without introducing provider or action authority.
technicalObjective: Implement exactly the two closed V1 schemas, runtime-safe semantic contract module, deterministic validator, documentation, state, and evidence defined by GOV-040; do not implement an IntelligenceProvider, model invocation, gateway, adapter, workflow, proposal generator, or executor.
architectureReferences: docs/architecture/source/Sri U-Thong Grand Hotel AI OS.md
assumptions: No production write, deployment, or live credential access is authorized.
Only prepared public or internal evidence is admitted; no guest, payment, booking, inventory, pricing-authority, credential, or secret data is in V1.

P2-001-R02 distinguishes structural schema validation from deep-module semantic enforcement; P2-002 preserves that boundary and never treats caller-supplied or schema-only analytics data as semantically authoritative.
Codex, OpenAI API, local models, and other future providers must implement the same port contract and cannot authorize an intervention.
A separate governance task must admit the exact validator command before P2-002 moves to ready.
acceptanceCriteria: Exactly two closed Draft 2020-12 structural authorities exist: `schemas/intelligence-provider-request-v1.schema.json` and `schemas/intelligence-provider-result-v1.schema.json`; every object sets `additionalProperties: false` and implements the exact V1 variants, fields, types, enums, and bounds in the GOV-040 design.

Exactly one runtime-safe semantic authority exists at `packages/ai-analysis-contracts/src/intelligence-provider-contracts-v1.mjs`; it exports only `validateIntelligenceRequest(input)` and `validateIntelligenceResult(input, request)`, internally loads committed schemas, accepts no caller-supplied authority or dependencies, returns frozen plain-data decisions, mutates no input, and never throws for any JavaScript input.

The request contract admits only bounded prepared public/internal evidence, the four exact purposes and analysis objectives, and closed allowed context. It exposes no prompt, schema, validator, provider option, storage location, policy, approval, capability token, command, or executable instruction.

The result contract has exactly `completed`, `insufficient_evidence`, `rejected`, and `provider_unavailable` variants; it implements the exact provider states, reason mappings, analysis shapes, cross-references, rank order, confidence bands, non-authority constants, and validation precedence in the GOV-040 design.

A `deterministic_analytics` item can cite only evidence produced through the canonical P2-001 public boundary under P2-001-R02 structural-plus-semantic assurance; P2-002 does not import calculator internals, recompute metrics, reorder identifiers, reinterpret reason codes, or accept replacement analytics schemas.

The conceptual `IntelligenceProvider.analyze(request) -> result` port remains unimplemented. Core contract logic imports no provider SDK, CLI, database, filesystem, network, environment, clock, queue, workflow, policy, approval, execution, verification, audit-storage, UI, or framework dependency; provider-specific behavior is deferred to adapters.

Malformed requests produce a schema-valid deterministic `rejected` decision before invocation; malformed provider results, missing internal authority, unsupported classifications, and every non-available provider state fail closed. No result grants authorization, approval, capabilities, execution, verification, or production eligibility.

`tests/ai-analysis/validate-intelligence-provider-contracts-v1.mjs` compiles both committed schemas against Draft 2020-12, verifies all finite variants and semantic rules, authority-replacement and self-authorization rejection, P2-001-R02 boundary preservation, frozen cloned outputs, and repeated adversarial never-throw behavior, and runs as `node tests/ai-analysis/validate-intelligence-provider-contracts-v1.mjs`.

Independent Sol QA confirms exact validator admission, deep-module and hexagonal boundaries, human-approval preservation, allowed paths, required tests, CI, rollback, and retained machine-readable evidence.
requiredChecks: Draft 2020-12 schema compilation and exact-variant validation
deep-module public-surface and hexagonal dependency validation
solEscalationTriggers: Any required change crosses the exact two schemas, one contract module, one validator, documentation, task, evidence, or monitored-risk paths.
Any caller/provider authority injection, schema/semantic drift, provider-specific import, or leakage of validation, storage, transport, or SDK internals arises.

Any production access, live/guest data, credential, payment, booking, inventory, pricing, database, RLS, migration, authorization, approval, execution, concurrency, or workflow-correctness ambiguity arises.
rollbackExpectations: Revert only the two P2-002 schemas, contract module, validator, documentation, task state, and P2-002 evidence; preserve P1/P2-001/P2-001-R02 authorities and historical evidence, canonical sources, immutable snapshot, and external systems.
